x.notes: insights[5] says 'the more refined a creature is, the more concentrated food it needs'; segs 514-516 say the more tamei ('tummy') one is, the more concentrated food is needed (inverted meaning, term misread); Yiddish repeatedly uses 'נתפעל געמאכט' for 'affected' (wrong sense), and stories[0].yi 'ניטאמאל אויב' for 'no matter whether' is unidiomatic; sources are thorough and correctly referenced (Rashi 7:23, 6:18, 7:12, Sanhedrin 108b, Vayikra 26:6 + Ramban, Ramban Bamidbar 14:9, Bereishis 16:12)

rationale: Neither side hallucinates; each has one unsupported claim (X inverts the tamei/concentrated-food point). In tier 2, Y has more term errors (2 vs 1, misreading Ribono shel Olam as the Ramban) and more source errors (2 vs 0, including Toras Kohanim). In tier 3, Y has 2 of 3 boundaries bad against 0 for X and misses about 5 sources that X lists correctly. Y's Yiddish is also clearly worse (6/10 bad vs 3/10).
